newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila seen buying more corn to ease shortage.
newsitem.headline: Manila seen buying more corn to ease shortage.

text.p: Philippine hog farmers are expected to shop for more corn in the coming week to meet short term requirements, Manila grains traders said on Friday.
Traders said they have received inquiries for imports of 25,000 tonnes yellow corn.

On Monday, feed millers and hog farmers bought 55,000 tonnes of U.S. number 2 yellow corn at $137.75 per tonne C&F. Continental Grains Co won the tender to supply the corn for July 10-25 arrival, they said.

Traders said domestic corn prices are firming since the bulk of the Philippine corn harvest is not due to start until July. Private firms have estimated the corn shortage this year at one to two million tonnes.

Corn users have asked the state-owned National Food Authority (NFA) in recent weeks to import 300,000 tonnes of corn before July. This is in addition to purchases made by the NFA so far this year -- 120,000 tonnes of yellow corn from China and 25,000 tonnes of U.S. white corn. The additional imports must be approved by President Fidel Ramos and Congress.
Meanwhile, wheat, soybean and soymeal buyers are expected to remain on the sidelines due to ample supply, traders said.
